claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system uses a gRNA to target and cleave DNA sequences with specificity.
source: The CRISPR/Cas9 system uses a gRNA to target and cleave DNA sequences with specificity, and can result in precise genome editing via homology directed repair (HDR) if a donor DNA template is simultaneously delivered along with the CRISPR/Cas9 system (Jinek et al., 2012; Cong et al., 2013; Cho et al., 2013; Mali et al., 2013a; DeWitt et al., 2016; Long et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work establishing this fundamental mechanism.

claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system can result in precise genome editing via homology directed repair (HDR) if a donor DNA template is simultaneously delivered along with the CRISPR/Cas9 system.
source: The CRISPR/Cas9 system uses a gRNA to target and cleave DNA sequences with specificity, and can result in precise genome editing via homology directed repair (HDR) if a donor DNA template is simultaneously delivered along with the CRISPR/Cas9 system (Jinek et al., 2012; Cong et al., 2013; Cho et al., 2013; Mali et al., 2013a; DeWitt et al., 2016; Long et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work on HDR-mediated genome editing.

claim: Extension of the gRNA with aptamer sequences can be used to recruit RNA binding counterparts within the cell that enable either the visualization or transcription of specific DNA sequences in the genome.
source: For example, extension of the gRNA with aptamer sequences can be used to recruit RNA binding counterparts within the cell that enable either the visualization or transcription of specific DNA sequences in the genome (Mali et al., 2013b; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work demonstrating aptamer-based gRNA extensions.

claim: Incorporation of modified RNA bases into the gRNA results in reduced immunogenicity, increased stability, and enhanced gene editing efficiency.
source: In addition, incorporation of modified RNA bases into the gRNA results in reduced immunogenicity, increased stability, and enhanced gene editing efficiency (Rahdar et al., 2015; Hendel et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work on modified RNA bases in gRNAs.

claim: Chemical modification of the donor DNA with phosphorothioates dramatically increases HDR efficiency by increasing donor DNA stability.
source: Finally, chemical modification of the donor DNA with phosphorothioates dramatically increases HDR efficiency by increasing donor DNA stability (Renaud et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work on phosphorothioate modifications.

claim: Very little is known about the chemical modifications that are tolerated by the gRNA of the CRISPR/Cas9 system and the donor DNA outside of base modifications and backbone modifications.
source: However, outside of base modifications and backbone modifications, very little is known about the chemical modifications that are tolerated by the gRNA of the CRISRP/Cas9 system and the donor DNA.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, representing a gap in existing research.

claim: It is uncertain if the gRNA of Cas9 and the donor DNA tolerate modifications with chemical moieties that are structurally unrelated to nucleotide bases.
source: In particular, it is uncertain if the gRNA of Cas9 and the donor DNA tolerate modifications with chemical moieties that are structurally unrelated to nucleotide bases, and how big these modifications can be without affecting the functionality of Cas9 or donor DNA.
evidence: This is a statement about uncertainty in the field, representing a knowledge gap.

claim: Nothing is known about the tolerance of the Cpf1 gRNA to chemical modifications.
source: In addition, nothing is known about the tolerance of the Cpf1 gRNA to chemical modifications.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of knowledge in the field.

claim: The gRNA and the donor DNA can be modified at their terminal positions with large modifications ranging from planar hydrophobic molecules to 35 kDa nucleic acids, without losing activity.
source: In this report, we investigated the types of synthetic modifications that the gRNA and donor DNA can tolerate in the CRISPR gene editing systems, and demonstrate that the gRNA and the donor DNA can be modified at their terminal positions with large modifications ranging from planar hydrophobic molecules to 35 kDa nucleic acids, without losing activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The crRNA for Cas9 tolerates large modifications at its 5' end.
source: Figure 2b demonstrates that the crRNA for Cas9 tolerates large modifications at its 5' end, and is less tolerant to modifications on the 3' end.

claim: crRNA with 3' modifications had a 50% reduction in NHEJ efficiency in cells.
